Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728

Record Class McpRequestState

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728.McpRequestState
Record Components:
continuation - The handler-opaque continuation value, exactly as thrown in McpInputRequiredSignal#getContinuation() (or, on a subsequent pause, exactly as the handler returned it a second time). Must be Juneau-marshallable (ordinary bean, Map, String, or similar). See the type-fidelity note above: it round-trips as generic JSON, not its original Java type.
method - The JSON-RPC method this state was sealed for (tools/call, prompts/get, or resources/read). Part of the AAD contract (see RequestStateCodec); also checked directly by the dispatcher against the follow-up request's own method as an extra sanity check.
round - The 1-based round counter: 1 on the first PAUSE, incremented on every subsequent PAUSE.
expiresAtMs - Absolute expiry timestamp in epoch milliseconds.
jti - A fresh, per-token random identifier minted on every PAUSE (see McpRevision#pause), used only to detect replay of THIS exact token. Opt-in: consulted by the dispatcher only when an operator has wired a ReplayCache via McpMrtrConfig.setReplayCache(ReplayCache); otherwise it rides in the sealed plaintext unused. Not wire-visible on its own — like every other field on this record, it only ever travels inside the opaque, AEAD-sealed requestState string.
argumentsHash - A canonical hash of the original request's arguments (RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme, then SHA-256, then base64url), captured at PAUSE time and re-verified against the RESUME request's own arguments on every subsequent round (see McpRevision#resolveMrtrContext). Always populated (unlike jti(), this check is not opt-in): a call with absent or empty arguments (for example resources/read's exact-path branch, which takes none) hashes the canonical empty object "{}" rather than leaving this field unset, so PAUSE and RESUME agree even when there is nothing to hash.
public record McpRequestState(Object continuation, String method, int round, long expiresAtMs, String jti, String argumentsHash) extends Record
The dispatcher-owned payload sealed into an opaque requestState token by RequestStateCodec.

Never wire-visible directly — InputRequiredResult.getRequestState() carries only the sealed string form. This type exists so the round counter (SEP-2322's max-rounds cap) and expiry travel *inside* the sealed token itself, per McpRevision's documented statelessness: no server-side session exists to hold them instead.

The sealed continuation is the only trusted per-round carrier. This is what makes it security-relevant: the continuation sealed here is authenticated (AEAD) and cannot be altered by the client between rounds, whereas the request arguments a handler sees on RESUME come from the follow-up request and are fully client-controlled (see McpMrtrResumeContext). Anything a handler must be able to trust across rounds — an authenticated principal, an authorization decision, a price, a resource id — must live inside this continuation, never be re-derived from the per-round arguments.

Continuation type fidelity. continuation is declared as Object because it is handler-opaque, but AeadRequestStateCodec.unseal(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.security.Principal) reconstructs it via generic JSON deserialization (Json.to(json, McpRequestState.class)). A handler that pauses with a Map or ordinary-bean continuation therefore gets back a generic JSON value on resume — a JsonMap/ JsonList/boxed primitive/String — never the original Java type. A handler that needs its original type back should not reconstruct it by hand: it retrieves the resume context from the BeanStore and calls McpMrtrResumeContext.continuationAs(Class), which converts the generic JSON value back to any Juneau-marshallable target type in one call.
